scope: CORRECTION from the user: the target is CODOL 3.19.26.22 / build 1649370, not 2697

target_clarified.server_role_of_2697: the codol_dedrun.exe under runs/2697-server-test is a borrowed protocol-compatible server, NOT the target version
target_clarified.why_it_works_at_all: the 1649370 client advertises shortversion 1.1.1.13 in connectResponse and the 2697 dedrun speaks the same 1.1.1.13 lineage (CODOL_Xor, seq-only netchan, 3-bit command stream), which is why challenge/connect/stats/gamestate complete
target_clarified.consequence: when we build our own server, its acceptance test is the 3.19.26.22 client, and the 2697 source is only a protocol reference for the shared 1.1.1.13 generation

new_reference_found.file: 他人文件参考/INTEL-native319-进大厅汇总.md
new_reference_found.what_it_is: a status report for someone else's Rust native319 server (16 modules, 5226 lines) serving CODOL 3.19.26.13 - the version immediately before ours
new_reference_found.verified_results_there: CS=9 (auth passed) + DW=5 (LSG alive) + SCENE=5, all achieved by server-side replies with zero client binary changes
new_reference_found.their_blocker: SCENE=6 (entering the lobby scene) is blocked because [lobby+0x1F4] becomes -2 every round, so the bdLobby state machine never completes a cycle

architecture.lsg.rs: LSG session: handshake, key derivation, 0x85 decrypt, task dispatch, heartbeat
architecture.ipc.rs: IPC bridge to a Python business side

what_we_can_reuse: the LSG auth frame layout and key derivation shape matches our server319.lsg and bdproto319.py, so those two agree
their port map is a checklist for a complete 3.19-class server
their SCENE=6 blocker is a known pitfall to expect on our side too
their zero-patch claim supports the approach of doing everything server-side
what_it_does_not_cover: it is a lobby/auth server, not an in-game server; nothing there about gamestate/snapshot/clc_move
it targets 3.19.26.13, so offsets and some payloads may differ from 3.19.26.22

revised_plan.step_1: keep server319.lsg as the auth/lobby side (it already reaches the lobby for our build)
revised_plan.step_2: build the in-game server ourselves against the 3.19.26.22 client, using runs/2697-native-src only as the 1.1.1.13 protocol reference
revised_plan.step_3: acceptance = the 3.19.26.22 client leaves loading and can stand/move; never use 2697 as the acceptance target
revised_plan.step_4: log everything from the first packet so version differences between 3.19.26.22 and 2697 show up immediately
